eras._note: 2016-10 to 2019 WordPress site (cherry.vc, launched 2016-11 with backdated posts; the 2015-2016 domain carried a WP 4.3 splash only): /portfolio/ renders one <li data-name data-invested(epoch seconds) id class=portolio-list-item> per company with a detail block (Launch year, 'Investment: Seed / Series A' stage label, founders, website) and an exit ribbon. The detail attributes are read into sources/site/portfolio-2016-2023.json (a file_list source); this era carries only name, slug and listing year. The January-2020 capture still carries this markup (the redesign landed 2020-02), so the era runs to 2020.

2020-2023 WordPress 5.x site: /portfolio/ renders one <div class='mix col-md-4 popup-trigger-thumnail <sector classes>' data-name data-chronological(investment year, sometimes yyyymmdd)> per company with hidden website / description / slug divs and an 'exited' logo class. Attributes read into sources/site/portfolio-2016-2023.json. The 2024 capture is the Next.js successor and matches nothing.
WordPress per-company pages (post type portfolio_item, 72-74 in the archived wp-sitemap); the Internet Archive captured only a handful, Common Crawl more (commoncrawl.company_paths).

2026 Webflow site: /founders lists 90 companies as links to /founder-companies/<slug>; names come from the live rendering (sources/site/webflow-companies.json). The 2024-2025 Next.js site (Sanity CMS, project 763y4e9t) rendered /founders from an RSC payload with no per-company URLs; that list surface is read live from the Sanity query API instead (sources/site/sanity-companies.json).

wayback._non_company_note: 'stealth' / 'stealth-3' are the 2018 listing's unnamed placeholders (no identifiable company: not rows, decisions.md D12); '48' is Flixbus's WordPress slug (portfolio_item/48) whose name the listing era already carries as 'Flixbus' / 'FlixMobility', dropped here so the per-company era cannot mint a row named '48'.

roster._note: Two people namespaces: /team_member/<slug> (WordPress 2020-2023, 22-25 pages in the archived wp-sitemap) and /team/<slug> (Webflow 2026). The Webflow namespace also carries the 'glimpse into our network' profiles (Pausder, Kuusi, Paananen, Engert, Goetze, Koc, Nothacker, Koehler: founders and operators in Cherry's LP and advisor network, never staff); they are dropped here so their names cannot attribute Form D seats. The 2016-2019 team listing pages had no per-person URLs, so those years are CURATED into sources/wayback/partner-roster.json from the archived /team/ captures and the firm's own hiring posts (decisions.md D10).

site_api._note: cherry.vc is a Webflow site (no public CMS API; escalation ladder step 5): the sitemap enumerates every /founder-companies/<slug>, /news/<slug> and /team/<slug> page and each page is fetched and read (webflow-companies.json, announcements-webflow.json, team-webflow.json). The 2024-2025 Next.js site's Sanity dataset (project 763y4e9t, production) is still publicly queryable and is read as a second, dated list surface. The archived 2016-2023 WordPress listings carry the firm's own investment dates, stage labels (2016-2019) and sector classes and are read into portfolio-2016-2023.json. talent.cherry.vc is a Getro job board (Thrive precedent).

edgar._note: Entity-qualified phrases only (PRO-73): the bare word drowns in Cherry Hill / Cherry Creek / Cherry AB / Cherry Bekaert. Measured 2026-09-04: EDGAR full-text search for "Cherry Ventures" over all years returns 5 documents, all Form D (the firm's own US feeders, Cherry Decentral I and the Titanbay feeders); no third-party registrant names the firm.

desks._note: Namesakes verified by entity and address (the firm is Linienstr. 214, 10119 Berlin), never by name: Cherry Tree Ventures IV, LP (Minnetonka MN, CIK 1380609; Section 16 filings 2006-2007) is an unrelated Minnesota fund; Cherry Ventures Ltd. (Companies House 06327834, London, incorporated 2007-07-30, Paul Street) predates the firm and is unrelated; the Titanbay Focused Master Fund feeders for Cherry Ventures Fund V / Select V (CIKs 2043309, 2040642, Luxembourg) are a third-party access platform's vehicles (external, decisions.md D5). The firm's own SEC entities: Cherry Ventures Management GmbH (AIFM) (CIK 1774845, ERA CRD 301494), Cherry Ventures Fund III (US), L.P. (1762608), Cherry Ventures Fund IV (US), L.P. (1898140), Cherry Decentral I GmbH & Co. KG (1908733).

profile._note: Three site vocabularies crosswalk to the closed taxonomy: the 2026 Webflow INDUSTRY strings, the 2024-2025 Sanity tags (Healthcare, Fintech, Deep Tech, Dev & Data Tools, Cyber, Climate, ...) and the 2020-2023 WordPress sector classes (consumer, fintech, healthtech, industry, lifestyle, mobility, saas, climate, interactive-entertainment). The Sanity 'Exit' tag is an outcome flag, not a sector, and is read into exit_tag. focus_min_companies ~4.5% of the expected ~150-row base. The Webflow INDUSTRY strings are comma-joined lists ('Industry, SaaS, AI'); the base joins sector sets with commas and the profile splits them again, so the single words (Industry, AI, B2B, Sustainability, Supply Chain) are crosswalked as well.

shape._note: Set to Cherry's own properties before the first milestone (PRO-73): a 2012-founded pre-seed/seed firm with a ~150-row book has a handful of $1B+ rows (Flix, Forto, Black Forest Labs, AUTO1 public, at most a few more), so the $1B+ share guard is halved from the 20% megafund default; a genuine seed book keeps the 80% C2A ceiling. S2A ceiling restated 2026-09-17 under the status contract (D-S2A in decisions.md): 112 seed entries, 9 censored, 51 undetermined, cohort 52 at 92.3% with 50.5% coverage. Cherry files no Form Ds, so every decision rests on a citation, and on a young European pre-seed book only about half the seeds have a reachable published record; the half that does is the half the press covered, which is the winners. The 80% ceiling was set expecting a genuine seed book to fall under it, but it was written against a cohort that included unverified rows. Restated to 0.95 with the coverage published beside the rate; the guard still fires above that.
